title: Transferable Graph Structure Learning for Graph-based Traffic Forecasting Across Cities

problem.claim: Accurate graph-based traffic forecasting requires sufficient traffic data, which may be unavailable in real-world applications.

gap.claim: Existing transfer methods use pre-defined graph structures that may be noisy or biased and can harm knowledge transfer.

contributions.claim: TransGTR jointly learns and transfers graph structures and forecasting models across cities.
TransGTR combines a node feature network, a structure generator, and a forecasting model, using knowledge distillation and temporal decoupled regularization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: On real-world traffic speed datasets, TransGTR outperformed state-of-the-art baselines by up to 5.4% under a fair comparison.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph-based deep learning is effective for spatio-temporal traffic forecasting.
Traffic data may be insufficient, motivating transfer from data-rich source graphs to data-limited target graphs.
Pre-defined graph structures used by existing methods may introduce noise or bias into transfer.
TransGTR jointly transfers learned graph structures and forecasting models using city-agnostic node features and temporal decoupled regularization.
The authors report up to 5.4% improvement over state-of-the-art baselines on real-world traffic speed datasets.

source_observation.claim: Learning transferable graph structures jointly with forecasting models is reported to improve cross-city traffic forecasting.

interpretation.claim: Transfer quality may depend on adapting the relational structure rather than transferring only model parameters.

application.claim: For graph-based forecasting across domains, consider learning transferable structures alongside the prediction model.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond traffic forecasting or the reported datasets.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, splits, and transfer settings are not specified.
The evaluation metric and statistical significance of the reported improvement are not specified.
Ablation results and implementation details are not provided.
